newsitem.title: USA: Haitian alleges sodomy by New York police.
newsitem.headline: Haitian alleges sodomy by New York police.

text.p: The New York police force, credited with bringing down crime but also blasted for alleged abuses of black and Hispanic suspects, was investigating two officers Wednesday on charges they sodomized a Haitian man with a toilet plunger.

Haitian immigrant Abner Louima was in critical condition in Coney Island Hospital after surgery to repair a pierced lower intestine and a torn bladder from the alleged assault Saturday in a Brooklyn precinct house bathroom.

Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, usually quick to defend officers, Wednesday called for the dismissal of the pair and jail time if the allegations were proven. He said the charges were being investigated by the New York Police Department and the Brooklyn District Attorney.

"If the allegations are true and substantiated then they should result in their dismissal and they should also result in receiving substantial terms of imprisonment," Giuliani said at his daily City Hall news conference.

Louima told investigators he was arrested outside a nightclub, pushed to the ground and handcuffed, kicked and beaten. He said the officers used racial slurs and told him, "you niggers have to learn to respect police officers."
The police were called to the nightclub over a fight Louima said he was not involved in. He was charged with assault and resisting arrest.

Louima, 30, said officers took him to the 70th precinct where he was strip-searched, marched into the bathroom and sodomized with the handle of a plunger. He said they also shoved the plunger in his mouth, breaking teeth.
Police Commissioner Howard Safir said two officers had been put on modified duty. He said they had three previous complaints against them that were not substantiated.
Fourteen months ago, Amnesty International human rights group said reports of brutality, shootings and deaths in custody had risen sharply in the country's biggest police department.

Amnesty and other groups say the victims are predominantly black and Hispanic and that alleged abuses continue. Police attribute a rise in complaints to more aggressive policing, which has contributed to the city's lowest crime rate in a generation.
